## Model carry-forward scope (resolved this round)

Two different things were being conflated under "the best-performing model": the
deployment question (which single model should actually be used) and the mechanism
question (do models differ in how much they rely on text vs. identity). They don't need
the same model set.

- **Single carried-forward model** (argmin 2019 AI MAE on the Evidence condition; CI-overlap
  tie prefers base): gets the full battery — Figures 1 (already), 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. This stays
  unchanged from the existing selection rule. If the winner turns out to be FT-raw, the
  anchoring-probe conditional promotion (F3 main text) still applies as the qualifier.
- **All three FT variants, plus base as the reference case**: get the salience-gap /
  re-identification machinery only (Figures 10, 11, 12) — required by R8's own wording
  ("FT-raw should replicate *the base model's* salience gap... FT-anon and FT-summ...
  should show a smaller gap"), which cannot be tested with a single model. This was already
  implicit in the pre-registered R8 text; it just wasn't reconciled with the "best-performing
  model only" framing that governs the rest of Part 2/3.
- This resolves the blind-spot concern directly: cross-model differences in anchoring
  reliance get tested (R8) without paying for the full name-swap / 2024-holdout / replication
  battery three or four times over.
- **`docs/experimental-design.md`'s Part 2 preamble still says "best-performing model only"
  throughout** — that line needs updating to reflect this split whenever the design doc gets
  its next pass. Not done yet; flagging so it doesn't silently drift out of sync with this doc.

**Compute note (2026-07-28):** inference on test runs has been fast, and there's
near-unrestricted access to 6 Grace Hopper H200 chips (low queue — ARM64 discourages
competitors from switching setups). This eases the resource constraint that originally
motivated keeping the full battery to one model. Worth revisiting whether to extend
Figures 5–9 to more than the single carried-forward model once this scope has been
stress-tested against actual wall-clock time on the H200s, rather than assuming the
original GW Pegasus A100 budget still binds.

## New / resolved hypotheses

**F2, resolved** (goes in Part 2, feeds Figure 3):

> On the Evidence condition (raw, named-entity-intact text) at inference — the hardest
> test, since only FT-raw trained on this exact distribution — AI MAE ranks
> `MAE(FT-summ:Evidence) < MAE(FT-anon:Evidence) < MAE(FT-raw:Evidence)`. Training on
> progressively de-identified text teaches the model to extract calibration signal from
> described conditions rather than country identity or content fingerprints; that skill
> transfers to reading raw text — a superset of what FT-anon/FT-summ trained on — more
> effectively than FT-raw's matched-distribution advantage, because part of that advantage
> is a name-conditioned shortcut (F3) rather than genuine calibration.
> - **Alternative**: the reverse ranking holds — matched-distribution incumbency dominates
>   the abstraction benefit. If this holds *and* F3/R8 show FT-raw's advantage is
>   substantially anchoring-driven, the best deployment model is also the least trustworthy
>   one for the Part 3 mechanism tests — the scenario the anchoring-probe promotion exists
>   to catch.
> - **Null**: no reliable ranking among the three FT variants on raw evidence —
>   training-representation effects wash out once real names are present in the input
>   regardless of training text.

*Open: does base belong in this ranking, or is its position handled separately by F1? Not
resolved yet.*

**R1 (was R10), the 2023 agreement test** — already drafted in `key-hypotheses.md`'s prior
discussion, carried here for reference:

> The carried-forward model's AI MAE, in its best (Evidence) condition, is at or below the
> human LOO MAE. If AI MAE ≤ human LOO MAE, the model deviates from panel consensus by no
> more than a typical human coder. Tested confirmatorily on 2023 data; the 2019 value
> appears only as the Figure 1 reference line, a diagnostic, not a registered 2019 test.

*Open: a 2019 counterpart hypothesis (draft label B7) was floated for symmetry — "the
carried-forward model's AI MAE is at or below the 2019 human LOO MAE (0.709)" — but the
conversation moved to the model-ranking hypothesis above as the headline B/F-adjacent item
instead. Not decided whether B7 still gets registered alongside it or is dropped in favor
of treating R1 as a standalone, non-replicated 2023 test. Flagging rather than choosing.*
